messages:
raj-oncall: :rotating_light: P1 alert — PelagoHealth dedicated canary (tenant pel-4321) started failing after pinned artifact rollout at ~12:03 UTC. Elevated 5xx and connection resets. Paging SRE.
incident-bot: Alert triggered: pelago-health.canary.error-rate > 15% for 3m. Pager: raj-oncall, liz-sre. Link: https://rwd/alert/AXYZ123
deploy-bot: Canary rollout: artifact pelago/serve:v3.2.4 pinned to pool pelago-dedicated-canary-1 at 12:01:07 UTC. Health checks passing initially.
raj-oncall: symptoms: 502/503 for streaming requests and some long hangs. Customer being impacted for small subset of traffic (canary slice). Need triage, isolate tenant if necessary.
ben.kim: seeing repeated runtime exceptions in inference runtime logs: "kv-cache-mismatch" followed by KILL of worker process. Looks like artifact v3.2.4 changed kvcache layout.
liz-sre: on it. can we divert canary traffic back to reserved pool and roll pinned artifact back to v3.2.3? Prefer surgical steps rather than full pool restart.
maya-cs: PelagoHealth CS is on standby. They reported increased error rate in production dashboards. Putting a heads-up to their eng now.
alice.pratt: tagging product/pg. Need impact estimate for SLA. How many requests affected? quick numbers please.
ben.kim: rough: canary slice ~5% of tenant pel-4321 traffic -> ~120 requests/min across pool. Error rate peaked at 22% in the last 3m.
raj-oncall: priority: isolate tenant, stop further pin propagation, revert artifact on canary, divert traffic to reserved pool. Sequence: 1) lock artifact (prevent further pins) 2) isolate tenant 3) pin previous artifact 4) divert traffic 5) validate 6) communicate.
liz-sre: starting isolation step now.
liz-sre: run: ```rwdctl tenant isolate --tenant pel-4321 --reason "canary-failure-pinned-v3.2.4"``` -> returns job id isolate-842
deploy-bot: Isolation job isolate-842 accepted. Observed connections draining.
ben.kim: copying recommended rollback command: ```rwdctl artifact pin --pool pelago-dedicated-canary-1 --artifact pelago/serve:v3.2.3 --force --note "rollback v3.2.4 -> v3.2.3 kvcache mismatch"```  Should be immediate for canary.
raj-oncall: @liz-sre please confirm before pinning. Also start traffic divert once pinned.
liz-sre: confirmed. pinning now.
deploy-bot: Pin job pin-221 created. Preflight checks: compatible kernels ok. Proceeding.
deploy-bot: pin-221 success. Canary pools now serving v3.2.3 for pinned slots.
ben.kim: good. next step divert tenant traffic: ```rwdctl route modify --tenant pel-4321 --from pool:pelago-dedicated-canary-1 --to pool:pelago-dedicated-reserved-2 --strategy gradual --weight 100 --note "surgical divert after pin rollback"```  Executing.
liz-sre: divert job route-909 accepted. Monitoring metrics.
raj-oncall: Maya, please tell PelagoHealth we are diverting their canary traffic to a reserved pool and rolling back pinned artifact. ETA ~5-8m to stabilize.
maya-cs: messaging draft to PelagoHealth: "We're seeing elevated errors for a small canary slice. We are diverting your traffic to a reserved pool and rolling back to the last known-good artifact. No data lost; expect recovery within 10 minutes. I'll update you in 5." Sending now.
thor-support: on-call for PelagoHealth. Confirm they acknowledged and paused internal deploys. They confirmed pause.
ben.kim: metrics: error rate dropping — now at 6% in the last 2m post-divert. latencies normalizing. CPU on canary pool still shows occasional OOM traces but traffic is offloading.
liz-sre: verifying tracing for sample failing requests. Root cause consistent with kv-cache layout mismatch in v3.2.4 -> causes worker to exit under load when streaming long contexts.
raj-oncall: ok contain step successful. Next: keep tenant isolated from canary pool for now, schedule full unpin and coordinate with model team to produce proper compatibility build.
alice.pratt: we need a follow-up action item to ensure artifact compatibility tests include kv-cache layout check. Assign to eng-ml and eng-runtime.
ben.kim: creating bug and rollout-blocker PR: https://git.rwd/pelago/issue/4821
deploy-bot: isolation job isolate-842 completed. tenant pel-4321 detached from pool pelago-dedicated-canary-1.
maya-cs: PelagoHealth responded: "Thanks — we see traffic drop and errors diminishing. Please let us know when it's fully stable and next steps for rollout." They asked for postmortem.
liz-sre: final checks: 15m after rollback, error rate for that tenant on production <0.5%. All streaming sessions restored via reserved pool. Marking incident mitigated.
raj-oncall: handing off to liz-sre for follow-up and postmortem. Please capture timeline, commands run, and customer comms.
liz-sre: taking handoff. I'll open incident ticket with timeline and action items. Immediate RCA: incompatible kv-cache layout in artifact v3.2.4. Suggested short-term mitigations: stricter artifact schema gating, cross-checks on pinned artifacts, and automated canary traffic kill switch.
alice.pratt: assign follow-ups: eng-runtime (ben.kim) for tests, eng-ml for artifact build gating, cs (maya-cs) to coordinate customer PM for postmortem.
maya-cs: scheduling customer call for 14:00 UTC to review and share RCA.
raj-oncall: closing pager. Great coordinated response. :thumbsup:
liz-sre: Incident ticket: INC-2026-042, timeline and commands attached. Will postmortem in #postmortems in 24h.
alice.pratt: add cost note: diverted traffic to reserved pool — track delta billing for PelagoHealth for the window.
thor-support: PelagoHealth confirms they are back to normal. Thank you team.
ben.kim: re: long-term: pushing artifact compatibility tests into CI and adding runtime flag to refuse incompatible KV caches. PR open: https://git.rwd/pull/9876
liz-sre: reaction :white_check_mark:
maya-cs: I'll follow up with the customer after PM + postmortem is ready.
raj-oncall: thanks everyone. I'll file a short blameless summary for execs.
